how_these_were_written: From how an operator actually asks after losing the thread of their own system: 'I forgot what it does', 'draw me how it fits together', 'what happens when someone pays'. 'explain this codebase like a picture' is kept and marked non-lexical: a person says it, and no honest description contains those words. The near-misses share real vocabulary with this description and belong elsewhere: adopting a diagram library (repo-triage), defining done for a map before building it (hsi-operator Door 2), saving architecture notes before compaction (context-steward), and fixing a webhook bug, which is code work and no skill.

cases.prompt: I've lost track of what our app actually does, can you map how it all works
build me a zoomable canvas of our architecture across these repos
what happens step by step when a user signs up and then a payment webhook fires
which feedback loops in this system are running away and which hold steady
give me an interactive map of how our services and infrastructure connect
map how our game works from a player's input to what they see
explain this codebase to me like a picture
is this diagram library worth adopting as a dependency
before we build the map, what does done mean for it
save the architecture notes before the context window is compacted
fix the bug in the webhook handler so the test passes
